text:
nina: Quick heads-up: rolling out a set of Billing Guardrails next Tuesday to reduce surprise invoices for small and PAYG accounts. Main points: 1) short "pacing windows" on sustained bursts (up to 30s), 2) free credit expiry shortened to 6 months with a one-time 30-day grace for current credits, 3) clearer invoice tags when pacing applied. Draft: https://redwood.internal/billing/guardrails

rahul: Will this change how tokens are billed?

nina: No — billing for completed tokens is unchanged. Pacing delays token generation; if we cause a failed completion we'll evaluate credits case-by-case. Finance will publish a short FAQ.

support: We'll add KB and canned replies. Suggest showing header detection so SDKs can react.

nina: We'll emit X-Redwood-Pacing: true and Pacing-Delay-Ms when active. Recommend clients use jittered backoff (start ~500ms). Example to include in KB:

```bash
curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
# look for: X-Redwood-Pacing: true
```

finance-bot: FYI: invoice line will show "Pacing Applied" when pacing materially affected request completion during the billing window. For disputed cases, open a billing ticket.

rahul: Rollout plan?

nina: Staged canary Mon 09:00 PT -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48h. Auto-abort on p99 latency regressions. Comms: targeted emails to impacted accounts, blog post, in-console banner.

support: ETA for KB and playbook: EOD today.

nina: TL;DR: Billing Guardrails = short pacing to protect latency, no billing model change, new headers + invoice tags, staged rollout. Feedback welcome. :wave:
